label: CONSTRUCTED COUNTERFACTUAL -- NOT MEASURED DATA
statement: This file is a labeled, deterministic transform of the observed EPA AQS hourly PM2.5 record for the Portland metro, September 2020 (parameter 88502). Every value is an observed value multiplied by a constant; every hour is an observed hour or a verbatim repeat of an observed whole day. It is NOT measured data: no monitor recorded these concentrations at these times, and it must never be plotted, cited, or pooled as observed air quality. It is NOT Los Angeles data and NOT Palisades data -- the geography, monitors, and diurnal structure are Portland's. Any 'Palisades-equivalent' framing is a SEVERITY ANALOGY ONLY, describing how bad and how long, not a claim about any particular fire or city.
severity_anchor: Scale 4.436 = 2496.1/562.7: the synthetic peak equals the worst VERIFIED hourly PM2.5 recorded over an intact, non-evacuated city - 2496.1 ug/m3 at Florey, Canberra, night of 5-6 Jan 2020, computed from the ACT Government's raw open-data hourly records (dataset 94a5-zqnn; the widely quoted ~5000 Canberra figure is an AQI index value, not a concentration). Documented all-source ceiling, cited but NOT scaled to: 5229 ug/m3 hourly at a Fort McMurray community site, May 2016 (Landis et al. 2018, doi 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.10.008), whose monitors sat in/adjacent to the burn perimeter of an evacuated town - breaking the sheltering-population premise this scenario models.
deterministic: no RNG, no clock; same inputs and arguments reproduce these bytes

checks.name: writer round-trips the observed CSV byte-identically
header line identical to the observed file
date/time formats are yyyy-MM-dd and HH:mm
file hour 0 timestamp matches the observed file
simulation anchor 2020-09-07T00:00 is inside the series
no NaN/gap hours in the Multnomah field
file hours contiguous with no gaps
pre-episode hours preserved exactly (scaled, not moved)
every value is scale x an observed value
